title: Generic restriction of continuous coefficient sections on a normal scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field at the generic point $\eta$, and $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ for the generic inclusion. Let $A$ be a nonarchimedean normed field, meaning a field with an absolute value satisfying $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$, and its metric topology. Put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$ for every scheme $T$, where $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for profinite $S$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical continuous-function realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization]. For every affine object $U\to X$ of the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $U_\eta=U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$. Restriction gives a bijection of rings
$$C(|U|,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|U_\eta|,A).$$
These bijections commute with every $X$-morphism between affine pro-etale objects, and with postcomposition by continuous field homomorphisms $A\to A'$. The empty object is included. No completeness or local compactness of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent extension of the normal generic-point argument: Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, and Theorem 2.3.4 (ind-etale refinement). Coefficient realization: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach, Example 3.1, p. 6. Discrete analogue: literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 09Z5, lemma-push-constant-sheaf-from-open (1). This norm-topology statement is not quoted as Tag 09Z5 itself.

proof.text: First record the chart geometry, without assuming $X$ affine or quasi-separated. If $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ is nonempty affine, $R$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], its prime localizations are the corresponding local rings of $X$, hence are normal by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] to see that $R$ is integrally closed in its fraction field. The generic point corresponds to $(0)$, so the same stalk-localization statement identifies this fraction field with $k$. Cover $U$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into such $V$. These form an open basis: shrink around the image point in $X$, then take an affine neighbourhood in its inverse image. By [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability] and the site definition, $W\to V$ is weakly etale. It therefore gives a weakly etale ring map $R\to B$ in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]; in particular $B$ is flat over $R$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $W_\eta$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_Rk)$ and its projection with the structural ring map.

source.place: Tag 092W, lemma-normality-goes-up, chart setup; Algebra Tag 030B; Schemes Tag 01I4

proof.text: On each chart from step 1 put $D=B\otimes_Rk$. This is the localization of $B$ at the images of $R\setminus\{0\}$: the maps sending $b\otimes(a/s)$ to $ab/s$ and $b/s$ to $b\otimes(1/s)$ are inverse by the tensor and localization relations. By [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain], a nonzero $s\in R$ acts injectively on $B$. The localization zero criterion then makes $B\to D$ injective. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-integral-closure] are now exactly satisfied. Every idempotent $e\in D$ is integral over $B$, since it solves the monic equation $T^2-T=0$; it consequently belongs to $B$, where injectivity gives the same idempotent equation and uniqueness of the lift. The correspondence of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] now proves that inverse image gives a bijection $\operatorname{Clop}(W)\to\operatorname{Clop}(W_\eta)$: $D(b)$ pulls back to $D(b\otimes1)$ by the definition of inverse image of a prime. This includes $B=0$, since then $D=0$ and both spectra are empty.

source.place: Tag 092W, lemma-normality-goes-up; idempotent application of Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition

proof.text: We globalize the clopen bijections, using only their uniqueness on the chart basis of step 1. Given a clopen $H\subset U_\eta$, extend $H\cap W_\eta$ uniquely to a clopen $H_W\subset W$ on every such chart. For two charts $W,W\prime$, cover their intersection by smaller chart-basis opens $Z$. The restrictions $H_W\cap Z$ and $H_{W\prime}\cap Z$ have the same generic inverse image $H\cap Z_\eta$, so step 2 on $Z$ makes them equal. Thus the $H_W$ agree on overlaps. Their union $\widetilde H\subset U$ is open, and its complement is open because on each $W$ it is $W\setminus H_W$. Its generic inverse image is $H$. Uniqueness holds by restricting any other extension to every $W$ and applying step 2. Hence inverse image along $i:U_\eta\to U$ is bijective on clopen subsets. This proof does not assume that intersections of affine opens of $X$ or $U$ are affine, or that the individual components of $U$ are open.

source.place: Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition, elementary open gluing after step 2

proof.text: The morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is affine: the inverse image of every nonempty affine open of the integral $X$ is all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and that of the empty open is empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $i:U_\eta\to U$ is affine and $U_\eta$ is affine. Both $U$ and $U_\eta$ are therefore qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and spectral by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral]. Apply [lem-sfb-spectral-clopen-component-homeomorphism] to their continuous map $i$ and the bijection proved in step 3. It yields a homeomorphism $h=\pi_0(i):P_\eta\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, where $P_\eta=\pi_0(U_\eta)$, $P=\pi_0(U)$, normalized by $h q_\eta=q i$. This remains valid for the empty object.

source.place: Tag 0906, lemma-spectral-pi0; agent clopen-preimage criterion; Morphisms Tag 01SD

proof.text: The field $A$ is totally disconnected. Indeed an ultrametric ball $B(a,r)$ is open and closed: if $y$ lies outside it, the ball $B(y,r)$ is disjoint from it by the strong triangle inequality. For distinct $a,b$, choose $0<r\leq |a-b|$; this clopen ball separates them. A connected subset cannot meet both a clopen set and its complement, so has at most one point. Any continuous $f:|U_\eta|\to A$ is therefore constant on every connected component: its image on that component is connected, as a separation of the image would pull back to a separation of the component. Thus $f=\bar f q_\eta$ for a unique function $\bar f:P_\eta\to A$. The quotient topology makes $\bar f$ continuous, since $q_\eta^{-1}(\bar f^{-1}(O))=f^{-1}(O)$ is open for every open $O\subset A$. The same factorization holds for continuous functions on $U$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, last paragraph; ultrametric total disconnectedness and quotient-topology argument expanded

proof.text: Define the extension of $f$ to be $E_U(f)=\bar f h^{-1}q$. It is continuous and $E_U(f)i=\bar f h^{-1}h q_\eta=f$. Conversely, if $g:|U|\to A$ is continuous, write $g=\bar g q$ as in step 5. Its restriction factors as $\bar g h q_\eta$, so applying the displayed formula returns $\bar g h h^{-1}q=g$. This proves bijectivity of the actual restriction map. Restriction preserves $0,1,+$ and multiplication pointwise; its inverse does too, since restriction is injective and the restrictions of $E_U(f+f\prime)$ and $E_U(f)+E_U(f\prime)$ are equal, and likewise for products and constants. For $U=\varnothing$, both function rings have one element and the same formula is the unique map.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, factorization through components; agent extension formula using step 4

proof.text: Let $v:V\to U$ be any $X$-morphism of affine pro-etale objects and $v_\eta:V_\eta\to U_\eta$ its base change. The projection equations give $iv_\eta=vi_V$. Thus $(g\circ v)\circ i_V=(g\circ i)\circ v_\eta$ for every continuous $g$ on $U$. This proves the restriction square commutes. In particular $E_U(f)\circ v$ and $E_V(f\circ v_\eta)$ have identical generic restrictions, so injectivity for $V$ proves they agree. For a continuous field homomorphism $a:A\to A\prime$, composition is continuous and $a\circ(g\circ i)=(a\circ g)\circ i$. This proves coefficient naturality of restriction. When both coefficient fields satisfy the statement, $a\circ E_U^A(f)$ and $E_U^{A\prime}(a\circ f)$ have the same generic restriction and hence agree by uniqueness for $A\prime$.

source.place: Fibre-product projection equations; elementary composition and uniqueness using step 6

proof.text: Finally use the canonical realization [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-field-continuous-realization] with the totally disconnected normed field $A$ established in step 5. It identifies the ring sheaf $R_{A,T}$ from [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with continuous functions on $T$ in precisely the topology supplied by [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Thus the ring bijections above concern the requested continuous coefficients and the actual restriction maps. All arguments used the norm topology itself; no completion, compactness of the coefficient field, or passage to discrete coefficients occurred.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.2.12; generic extension argument supplied by Q05 using Stacks Tags 092W, 00EE, 030B and 0906

lean.statement: theorem normal_generic_continuous_sections (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hnormal : ∀ x : X, IsDomain (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (A : Type v) [NormedField A] [IsUltrametricDist A] : (∀ (U : X.ProEt), IsAffine U.left → Function.Bijective (ContinuousMap.compRightAlgHom ℤ A (pullback.fst U.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).base.hom).toRingHom) ∧ (∀ (U V : X.ProEt), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → ∀ (f : V ⟶ U) (g : C(U.left, A)), (g.comp f.left.base.hom).comp (pullback.fst V.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).base.hom = (g.comp (pullback.fst U.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).base.hom).comp (((Over.pullback (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).map ((Scheme.ProEt.forget X).map f)).left.base.hom)) ∧ (∀ (A' : Type w) [NormedField A'] [IsUltrametricDist A'] (a : A →+* A') (ha : Continuous a) (U : X.ProEt), IsAffine U.left → ∀ g : C(U.left, A), (a.compLeftContinuous U.left ha g).comp (pullback.fst U.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).base.hom = a.compLeftContinuous ↥(pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) U.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))) ha (g.comp (pullback.fst U.hom (X.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint X))).base.hom))
